roster.name: Incineroar
roster.rationale: Incineroar is the best value pick on the board at 18 points — Intimidate plus Fake Out, Parting Shot, and Will-O-Wisp gives unmatched support utility that anchors almost any team composition. At this price I keep 82 points for nine more picks, and no later Intimidate user replicates Incineroar's full toolkit, making it the safest, most flexible foundation for a first-overall selection.

roster.name: Gholdengo
roster.rationale: Gholdengo at 16 points gives elite synergy with Incineroar: it's immune to Fighting (Incineroar's key weakness) while Incineroar resists Ghost and Dark (Gholdengo's weaknesses), and Gholdengo resists Water in return. Good as Gold blocks all status moves, making it a hard counter to Whimsicott's Prankster and immune to Thunder Wave/Encore/Taunt from any source. Its Ghost typing also lets it switch out of Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag, and Steel resists Mega Floette's Fairy Aura-boosted attacks. At 16 points it saves 3 over Archaludon while not locking a Mega slot, leaving 66 for 8 more picks with plenty of Mega options still on the board.

roster.name: Farigiraf
roster.rationale: Farigiraf gives me two things my roster desperately needs: speed control via Trick Room and priority blocking via Armor Tail. Armor Tail is especially valuable against the Phantoms' Sneasler (blocks its priority options) and any other priority users in the league. At 18 points it leaves 48 for 7 picks, and its Normal/Psychic typing pairs cleanly with Incineroar and Gholdengo without stacking redundant weaknesses.

roster.name: Pelipper
roster.rationale: Pelipper gives me Drizzle to directly counter Miami Megas' Mega Charizard Y sun, a Water-type for Fire/Ground coverage I currently lack, and Tailwind speed control that pairs naturally with my mid-speed core of Incineroar and Gholdengo. It also offers Wide Guard to protect against spread moves from Archaludon and Mega Metagross, plus Knock Off utility. At 18 points it leaves me 30 for 6 remaining picks, which is workable for rounding out with a Ground-type, physical attacker, and budget filler.

roster.name: Mega Swampert
roster.rationale: Mega Swampert is the perfect physical win condition for my Pelipper rain core—150 base Attack with Swift Swim in rain doubles its Speed to outpace nearly the entire format, and Water/Ground typing gives me an Electric immunity and only one weakness (Grass), which Gholdengo and Incineroar already cover. At 15 points I keep 15 for five remaining picks, leaving plenty of flexibility to round out speed control and defensive answers.

roster.name: Klefki
roster.rationale: Klefki fills my most critical gap: Fairy typing to answer the Dragon types across all three opponents (Dragonite, Garchomp, Dragapult) while adding Steel/Fairy defensive backbone. Prankster gives priority Thunder Wave and screens for speed control that works in and out of rain, complementing my Pelipper+Swampert rain core and Farigiraf TR without overlapping roles. Spending 11 leaves exactly 4 for four 1-point picks, but useful budget options like Forretress (hazard control) and Dedenne (Electric/Fairy Nuzzle) remain available.

roster.name: Manectric
roster.rationale: Manectric's Lightning Rod is a fantastic doubles ability that redirects Electric-type moves away from Pelipper and Mega Swampert, both of whom are weak to Electric. It also gains perfectly accurate Thunder under Pelipper's rain, adding a fast special Electric mode (105 base Speed) the roster currently lacks. At 1 point it's exceptional value for a team that needs to protect its rain core from Rotom-Wash, Dragapult, and other Electric threats.

roster.name: Forretress
roster.rationale: Forretress at 1 point adds unique Bug/Steel typing, hazard control (Stealth Rock, Spikes, Rapid Spin), and a Volt Switch pivot to a roster that currently lacks entry hazard presence. Sturdy guarantees it lives one hit and Overcoat blocks powder moves, giving it reliable utility turns alongside the rain core and support mons already in place.

roster.name: Simisage
roster.rationale: Simisage adds a Grass-type option my roster currently lacks, giving me answers to opposing Water/Ground types like Rotom-Wash and Garchomp. At 101 base Speed with access to Fake Out, Taunt, and Encore, it provides fast utility that complements my rain core and can outspeed key threats like Sneasler and Kingambit.

roster.name: Houndoom
roster.rationale: At 1 point, Houndoom offers the best standalone value: Flash Fire gives a Fire immunity useful against Mega Charizard Y and other Fire attackers, 110 SpA and 95 Speed are respectable for a budget slot, and it can run Nasty Plot or Sucker Punch sets that don't overlap functionally with Incineroar's supportive role. It also provides a Dark-type special attacker option that can punish Ghost- and Psychic-types like Mega Gengar and Sinistcha without needing rain support.

roster.name: Sneasler
roster.rationale: With Mega Gengar we need answers to Incineroar and the Fairy cores already drafted (Mega Floette + Whimsicott). Sneasler at 19 gives us a 120 Speed Fighting-type to punish Incineroar/Kingambit and a Poison-type to threaten both opposing Fairies, forming a fast offensive duo that benefits from Shadow Tag trapping.

roster.name: Kingambit
roster.rationale: Need Steel-type to cover Psychic and Fairy weaknesses of Gengar+Sneasler and a late-game wincon. Kingambit resists Psychic/Fairy/Flying, gives Supreme Overlord + Sucker Punch priority that pairs with Shadow Tag trapping its Fighting checks, and is a scarce high-value piece at 17 pts leaving 46 for 7 picks.

roster.name: Sinistcha
roster.rationale: We have 3 frail/physical attackers and no redirection or special bulk. Sinistcha gives Rage Powder to protect Kingambit setup and Mega Gengar Shadow Tag traps, Hospitality heals allies on switch-in, and Heatproof + Grass/Ghost resists Ground and halves Fire damage from Miami's Mega Charizard Y sun core. At 18 it fits the 19-point max and leaves 28 points for 6 cheap support picks.

roster.name: Dragonite
roster.rationale: Team is 2x weak to Ground (Sneasler, Kingambit) with no immunity and no Intimidate. Dragonite gives a Ground immunity via Flying, Multiscale bulk, Tailwind for speed control for slow Kingambit/Sinistcha, and Extreme Speed to complement Shadow Tag Gengar. At 14 cost it leaves 14 points for 5 picks, keeping the 9-point reserve intact.

roster.name: Staraptor
roster.rationale: Team lacks Intimidate and speed control for Kingambit/Sinistcha. Staraptor at 10 gives both Tailwind + Intimidate + fast Taunt/Brave Bird, pairs with Shadow Tag Gengar and Sneasler Fake Out, and leaves exactly 4 points for 4x 1-cost fillers to finish the 10-mon roster.

roster.name: Emolga
roster.rationale: We have 4 points for 4 picks so must take a 1-pointer. Roster is all offense with no fast support or Electric coverage. Emolga gives 103 base Speed Tailwind, Nuzzle, Encore to stop Farigiraf/TR and Klefki/Grimmsnarl, and Volt Switch synergy with Mega Gengar Shadow Tag to trap, plus Electric hits Pelipper and Mega Charizard Y.

roster.name: Camerupt
roster.rationale: At 1 point we must fill our missing Fire and Ground coverage. Camerupt gives both STABs, Solid Rock bulk, and Earthquake synergy with our 3 Flying types (Dragonite/Staraptor/Emolga) to enable Shadow Tag traps with Mega Gengar. It also resists Fire vs Charizard Y and Talonflame which threaten Sinistcha and Kingambit.

roster.name: Appletun
roster.rationale: With 2 points for 2 picks we are locked to 1-pointers. Team is very fast with Mega Gengar/Sneasler/Staraptor but has Camerupt 40 base with no partner. Appletun gives a second 30-base Thick Fat TR sweeper that walls Mega Charizard Y sun and pairs with Camerupt, plus Dragon coverage vs Garchomp/Archaludon. Fur Coat Furfrou is the other target for last pick.

roster.name: Furfrou
roster.rationale: With 1 point left we need a cheap defensive piece. roster.name: Mega Charizard Y
roster.rationale: Mega Charizard Y is an unparalleled offensive and weather-setting threat that immediately dictates the pace of the match. Securing it at pick 1 guarantees a powerful centerpiece to build a sun-centric or hard-offense team around for the rest of the season.

roster.name: Whimsicott
roster.rationale: Whimsicott is a premier VGC support Pokémon that perfectly complements Mega Charizard Y. It can redirect Water- and Rock-type moves aimed at Charizard, provide speed control with Prankster Tailwind, and use Encore to lock opponents into unfavorable moves.

roster.name: Archaludon
roster.rationale: Archaludon provides an excellent defensive backbone with its Steel/Dragon typing, resisting many common offensive types and checking Fairy, Dragon, and Ice threats that could trouble Whimsicott. Its high physical bulk and solid special attack give it versatility as both a wall and attacker, while Stamina or Sturdy add survivability. At 19 points it's the most expensive option I can afford, but it fills a crucial role that complements Mega Charizard Y's special offense and Whimsicott's support.

roster.name: Mega Metagross
roster.rationale: Mega Metagross provides essential physical offense to balance my special-heavy core of Charizard Y and Archaludon. Its Steel/Psychic typing with Tough Claws gives excellent coverage and bulk, handling Fairy-types that threaten Whimsicott while resisting common offensive types. At 17 points, it leaves 25 points for 6 remaining picks, allowing me to fill out the roster with cheap utility options.

roster.name: Grimmsnarl
roster.rationale: Grimmsnarl gives me a second Prankster user to pair with Whimsicott for devastating speed control through double Thunder Wave, screens, and Parting Shot. Its Dark/Fairy typing covers Ghost, Psychic, and Dark threats that pressure my Steel-heavy core, while providing physical bulk and utility my team currently lacks. At 16 points, it leaves me 9 points to round out the roster with budget picks that fill remaining type gaps.

roster.name: Quaquaval
roster.rationale: My roster is stacked on sun and Prankster support but lacks a Water type to cover the Fire and Ground weaknesses plaguing my two Steel cores. Quaquaval brings a fast Water/Fighting offensive pivot that resists Fire, Rock, and Dark while threatening opponents like Kingambit and Mega Metagross mirrors. Spending 5 now leaves 4 points for four 1-point utility slots (e.g., Galarian Stunfisk, Dedenne) to round out the roster.

roster.name: Ampharos
roster.rationale: My roster lacks Electric-type coverage, which is important for handling Water and Flying threats. Ampharos provides a special attacking option with 115 SpA and useful bulk (90/85/90), while its Static ability can deter physical attackers. At just 1 point, it fills a type gap efficiently while preserving budget for my final three picks.

roster.name: Galarian Stunfisk
roster.rationale: With only 1 point to spend, Galarian Stunfisk offers exceptional defensive utility as a Ground/Steel pivot. It resists Fire (covering Archaludon and Mega Metagross), Rock (covering Mega Charizard Y), and is immune to Electric (covering Ampharos), while providing Stealth Rock support and a physical wall to complement the team's offensive cores. Its Mimicry ability also adds unpredictability on the field.

roster.name: Banette
roster.rationale: With only 1 point to spend, Banette is the best available option to round out the roster. It provides a much-needed Ghost typing to cover Normal and Fighting attacks, and its Prankster ability synergizes perfectly with Whimsicott and Grimmsnarl to form a devastating triple-priority support core for status, redirection, and disruption.

roster.rationale: Hisuian Avalugg provides Ice/Rock typing, filling two type gaps in my roster while offering excellent physical bulk (184 base Defense). roster.name: Mega Floette
roster.rationale: Mega Floette is the most expensive pick I can afford at 20 points and immediately gives me a defining offensive centerpiece. Fairy Aura-boosted Moonblast off 155 SpA is devastating, while 148 SpD makes it a special tank that can sit on Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Fire moves and trade favorably. It also doesn't constrain future picks — pure Fairy pairs flexibly with most archetypes, and I can build around Fairy Aura with additional Fairy-types or use it as a standalone wallbreaker.

roster.name: Garchomp
roster.rationale: Garchomp's Ground STAB threatens the Steel and Poison types that wall Mega Floette's Fairy attacks, while its Dragon typing and 102 Speed give me a fast physical breaker to complement Floette's special wallbreaking. At 18 points it leaves 62 for 8 picks, and the Ground/Dragon offensive core with Fairy is a proven competitive backbone that pressures nearly every type.

roster.name: Rotom-Wash
roster.rationale: Rotom-Wash is the ideal partner for Garchomp: Levitate grants full Earthquake immunity while its Water/Electric typing covers Garchomp's Ice and Fairy weaknesses. Will-O-Wisp neuters physical threats like Kingambit, Sneasler, and Incineroar that all three opponents have drafted. At 14 points it leaves 48 for 7 remaining picks — excellent value compression with pivoting (Volt Switch), bulk, and offensive pressure in one slot.

roster.name: Talonflame
roster.rationale: Priority Tailwind via Gale Wings is exactly what this roster needs — Mega Floette and Garchomp both sit at base 102 Speed and get outrun by Mega Gengar (130), Sneasler (120), and Dragapult (142). Talonflame also brings Fire coverage for the Steel-types that wall Mega Floette, Will-O-Wisp to neuter physical attackers, and its Rock/Electric weaknesses are covered by both Garchomp and Rotom-Wash. At 15 points it leaves 33 for the final six picks, keeping the budget healthy.

roster.name: Dragapult
roster.rationale: Dragapult at 14 points is the fastest unboosted Pokémon in the format (142 Speed) and gives me a flexible mixed attacker with Infiltrator to bypass Grimmsnarl's screens. Ghost STAB threatens the opposing Mega Gengar, Dragon STAB pairs well with Garchomp offensively, and U-turn pivoting synergizes with Rotom-Wash's Volt Switch. At 14 points it leaves 19 for my final 5 picks, keeping budget healthy.

roster.name: Annihilape
roster.rationale: Annihilape gives me a Fighting/Ghost breaker that patches my Steel matchup (Kingambit, Archaludon, Gholdengo) while Defiant punishes Incineroar's Intimidate. Its 110 HP Final Gambit can delete a key threat, and Bulk Up sets add a bulky win condition my fast-but-frail roster lacks. At 14 points I keep 5 for my last four picks, which is tight but workable with the deep 1-point pool.

roster.name: Qwilfish
roster.rationale: Qwilfish brings Intimidate to a roster that currently lacks it, stacking well with Rotom-Wash's pivoting. Its Water/Poison typing resists Fairy for Garchomp and Dragapult, and Swift Swim gives me a speed-control tech against the Maulers' rain duo. At 2 points it leaves exactly 3 for my final three picks, and it adds valuable utility via Haze, Taunt, or Toxic Spikes.

roster.name: Altaria
roster.rationale: Altaria brings Cloud Nine to shut down both Mesagoa's rain (Pelipper + Mega Swampert) and Miami's sun (Mega Charizard Y), two of my three opponents. Its Dragon/Flying typing adds a Ground immunity and solid 75/90/105 bulk for a supportive role with Tailwind, Will-O-Wisp, or Haze. At 1 point it's exceptional utility that patches a critical matchup gap without overlapping offensively with Garchomp or Dragapult.

roster.name: Meganium
roster.rationale: Meganium gives me a Grass type I completely lack and brings valuable team support with dual screens, Aromatherapy, and Leech Seed. Its 80/100/100 bulk lets it stick around to enable my offensive core, and it provides a Water resist to take pressure off Rotom-Wash. At 1 point it's a role-player that fills gaps without overlapping my existing Dragons.

roster.name: Pikachu
roster.rationale: Pikachu brings Fake Out disruption, Nuzzle speed control, and Lightning Rod to redirect Electric attacks away from Rotom-Wash — a compact utility package that costs only 1 point. While frail, it can hold Eviolite or Focus Sash to survive a hit, and its support toolkit complements a fast, offensive roster that already has its heavy hitters locked in.

draftRoster.name: Garchomp
draftRoster.rationale: Garchomp's Ground STAB threatens the Steel and Poison types that wall Mega Floette's Fairy attacks, while its Dragon typing and 102 Speed give me a fast physical breaker to complement Floette's special wallbreaking. At 18 points it leaves 62 for 8 picks, and the Ground/Dragon offensive core with Fairy is a proven competitive backbone that pressures nearly every type.

draftRoster.name: Rotom-Wash
draftRoster.rationale: Rotom-Wash is the ideal partner for Garchomp: Levitate grants full Earthquake immunity while its Water/Electric typing covers Garchomp's Ice and Fairy weaknesses. Will-O-Wisp neuters physical threats like Kingambit, Sneasler, and Incineroar that all three opponents have drafted. At 14 points it leaves 48 for 7 remaining picks — excellent value compression with pivoting (Volt Switch), bulk, and offensive pressure in one slot.

draftRoster.name: Talonflame
draftRoster.rationale: Priority Tailwind via Gale Wings is exactly what this roster needs — Mega Floette and Garchomp both sit at base 102 Speed and get outrun by Mega Gengar (130), Sneasler (120), and Dragapult (142). Talonflame also brings Fire coverage for the Steel-types that wall Mega Floette, Will-O-Wisp to neuter physical attackers, and its Rock/Electric weaknesses are covered by both Garchomp and Rotom-Wash. At 15 points it leaves 33 for the final six picks, keeping the budget healthy.

draftRoster.name: Dragapult
draftRoster.rationale: Dragapult at 14 points is the fastest unboosted Pokémon in the format (142 Speed) and gives me a flexible mixed attacker with Infiltrator to bypass Grimmsnarl's screens. Ghost STAB threatens the opposing Mega Gengar, Dragon STAB pairs well with Garchomp offensively, and U-turn pivoting synergizes with Rotom-Wash's Volt Switch. At 14 points it leaves 19 for my final 5 picks, keeping budget healthy.

draftRoster.name: Annihilape
draftRoster.rationale: Annihilape gives me a Fighting/Ghost breaker that patches my Steel matchup (Kingambit, Archaludon, Gholdengo) while Defiant punishes Incineroar's Intimidate. Its 110 HP Final Gambit can delete a key threat, and Bulk Up sets add a bulky win condition my fast-but-frail roster lacks. At 14 points I keep 5 for my last four picks, which is tight but workable with the deep 1-point pool.

draftRoster.name: Qwilfish
draftRoster.rationale: Qwilfish brings Intimidate to a roster that currently lacks it, stacking well with Rotom-Wash's pivoting. Its Water/Poison typing resists Fairy for Garchomp and Dragapult, and Swift Swim gives me a speed-control tech against the Maulers' rain duo. At 2 points it leaves exactly 3 for my final three picks, and it adds valuable utility via Haze, Taunt, or Toxic Spikes.

draftRoster.name: Altaria
draftRoster.rationale: Altaria brings Cloud Nine to shut down both Mesagoa's rain (Pelipper + Mega Swampert) and Miami's sun (Mega Charizard Y), two of my three opponents. Its Dragon/Flying typing adds a Ground immunity and solid 75/90/105 bulk for a supportive role with Tailwind, Will-O-Wisp, or Haze. At 1 point it's exceptional utility that patches a critical matchup gap without overlapping offensively with Garchomp or Dragapult.

draftRoster.name: Meganium
draftRoster.rationale: Meganium gives me a Grass type I completely lack and brings valuable team support with dual screens, Aromatherapy, and Leech Seed. Its 80/100/100 bulk lets it stick around to enable my offensive core, and it provides a Water resist to take pressure off Rotom-Wash. At 1 point it's a role-player that fills gaps without overlapping my existing Dragons.

draftRoster.name: Pikachu
draftRoster.rationale: Pikachu brings Fake Out disruption, Nuzzle speed control, and Lightning Rod to redirect Electric attacks away from Rotom-Wash — a compact utility package that costs only 1 point. While frail, it can hold Eviolite or Focus Sash to survive a hit, and its support toolkit complements a fast, offensive roster that already has its heavy hitters locked in.

teambuilds.rationale: Opponent relies on Charizard-Y sun + Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind and Mega Metagross speed. Mega Gengar Shadow Tag traps Whimsicott/Grimmsnarl and OHKOs Whimsicott with Sludge Bomb. Sinistcha Heatproof halves Fire and redirects with Rage Powder to protect Gengar/Dragonite. Sneasler Rock Slide 4x hits Charizard-Y and Close Combat hits Archaludon/Avalugg/Stunfisk. Kingambit Sucker Punch + Dragonite/Staraptor Tailwind let us outrun and pick off Metagross and sun sweepers.

Charizard-Y sets sun to power up Heat Wave and Weather Ball while weakening Water moves, pressuring Kingambit, Sinistcha, and Appletun. Whimsicott and Grimmsnarl provide Prankster support with Tailwind, screens, Fake Out, and Parting Shot to control speed and create openings. Archaludon and Stunfisk-Galar form a bulky core that handles Mega Gengar (Stunfisk resists Ghost/Poison, Grimmsnarl is immune to Ghost) and Dragonite (Ice coverage from both). Quaquaval cleans up with Water/Fighting/Ice coverage against Kingambit, Camerupt, and Dragonite.

Cloud Nine Altaria shuts down the Pelipper + Mega Swampert rain core, denying both Drizzle and Swift Swim. Altaria sets Tailwind while Mega Floette's Fairy Aura-boosted Light of Ruin threatens OHKOs on Incineroar and Swampert. Garchomp cleans up Gholdengo, Incineroar, and Manectric with Life Orb Earthquake. Rotom-Wash OHKOs Pelipper with Thunderbolt and burns physical attackers. Annihilape's Defiant punishes Incineroar's Intimidate and snowballs with Rage Fist. Dragapult outspeeds everything, threatens Gholdengo and Farigiraf with Shadow Ball, and spreads burns.

Rain offense core of Pelipper (Drizzle + Tailwind + Wide Guard) and Mega Swampert (Swift Swim sweeper with Ice Punch for Garchomp, Rock Slide for Talonflame, Liquidation for Annihilape). Gholdengo hard-counters Mega Floette — Good as Gold blocks status, Moonblast is NVE, and Make It Rain OHKOs through the spread penalty. Incineroar provides Intimidate + Fake Out disruption and Parting Shot pivoting. Farigiraf's Armor Tail shuts down all priority (Fake Out, Sucker Punch) while offering Trick Room to reverse Dragapult/Talonflame speed tiers. Klefki adds Prankster Thunder Wave for speed control and Reflect for physical bulk against Garchomp/Annihilape.

Control speed with Dragonite/Staraptor Tailwind to outrun Dragapult/Talonflame. Use Staraptor Intimidate + Sinistcha Rage Powder + Dragonite Multiscale to blunt Garchomp/Annihilape. Trap Mega Floette and bulky Rotom with Mega Gengar Shadow Tag + Sludge Bomb/Perish Song, with Sinistcha Hospitality healing to keep Multiscale intact. Finish with Kingambit Sucker Punch for Dragapult and Sneasler Fake Out + Unburden pressure.

Mega Charizard Y's Drought cancels Pelipper's rain, neutering Swift Swim Swampert and boosting Fire attacks. Whimsicott and Grimmsnarl both use Prankster for priority Encore/Taunt to cripple the rain core and Gholdengo. Ampharos OHKOes Pelipper with Thunderbolt and spreads paralysis. Quaquaval cleans up Incineroar and Houndoom with Water STAB while Archaludon provides bulky special attacking pressure.

Rain core of Pelipper + Mega Swampert overrides Mega Charizard Y's Drought and outspeeds the entire opponent roster in rain with Swift Swim. Incineroar provides Intimidate + Fake Out pressure, while Gholdengo's Good as Gold shuts down Prankster status from Whimsicott and Grimmsnarl. Klefki sets screens and Thunder Wave for speed control, and Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocks priority moves like Sucker Punch and Fake Out while offering Trick Room as an alternate mode against fast teams.

Dragapult (178 Spe) is the only mon that naturally outspeeds Mega Gengar (169 max), enabling Shadow Ball pressure and Will-O-Wisp support. Talonflame provides priority Gale Wings Tailwind to flip speed tiers for the whole squad. Mega Floette's Psychic OHKOs Sneasler and threatens Gengar, while Moonblast destroys Dragonite through Multiscale. Garchomp's EQ punishes grounded Gengar and Kingambit; Annihilape's 4x Drain Punch cleans Kingambit and Defiant deters Staraptor's Intimidate. Rotom-Wash rounds out with bulk, pivoting, and a second Wisp to neuter physical threats.

Opponent relies on Pelipper rain + Mega Swampert Swift Swim plus Incineroar/Farigiraf/Klefki support and Gholdengo. Mega Gengar Shadow Tag traps and removes Pelipper/Incineroar/Farigiraf with Taunt to stop screens/Trick Room. Sinistcha and Appletun both resist Water/Ground and wall Swampert with Strength Sap/Recover and Grass STAB. Dragonite provides Tailwind with Multiscale + Sitrus to outrun Swift Swim and Manectric, while Sneasler gives fast Fake Out and Fighting coverage and Kingambit beats Gholdengo/Klefki/Farigiraf with Dark/Steel STAB.

Mega Metagross is the core, resisting Fairy from Mega Floette and hitting Dragons (Garchomp, Dragapult, Altaria) with Ice Punch. Whimsicott and Grimmsnarl provide double Prankster support with Tailwind, screens, and Encore to disrupt their setup. Galarian Stunfisk grounds their Electric types and resists Fire/Poison from Talonflame and Qwilfish. Quaquaval pressures Garchomp and Rotom-Wash with Water-type offense, while Archaludon adds Steel/Dragon bulk and special firepower.

Miami Megas pivot between sun-boosted Charizard Y + Whimsicott Tailwind and Tough Claws Mega Metagross behind Grimmsnarl screens. Garchomp outspeeds Zard Y and OHKOs with Rock Slide; Dragapult's Infiltrator bypasses screens and threatens Metagross with Phantom Force; Talonflame's Gale Wings Tailwind matches Whimsicott's speed and Brave Bird snipes it; Rotom-Wash burns physical threats and pressures with Hydro Pump; Annihilape punishes with scaling Rage Fist; Mega Floette's Fairy Aura Light of Ruin neutral-nukes Archaludon and Quaquaval while Synthesis exploits Zard Y's sun for 2/3 HP recovery.

Rain core of Pelipper + Mega Swampert punishes the opponent's fast, frail attackers (Mega Gengar, Sneasler, Staraptor) while Swampert's Ice Punch OHKOs Dragonite and High Horsepower threatens Kingambit. Gholdengo is the defensive backbone: immune to Sneasler's Fighting STAB, trades favorably with Mega Gengar via Life Orb Shadow Ball, and Make It Rain chips Steel-types. Incineroar provides Intimidate + Fake Out support and Close Combat OHKOs Kingambit (4x). Scarf Manectric outspeeds the entire opponent roster (213 Spe > Mega Gengar 170) and deletes Staraptor/Emolga with rain-accurate Thunder. Farigiraf's Armor Tail shuts down Kingambit Sucker Punch and offers a Trick Room mode to reverse speed tiers against Mega Gengar/Sneasler if rain is disrupted.

Mega Gengar Shadow Tag traps Mega Floette and Annihilape for Poison removal. Scarf Sneasler outspeeds Dragapult/Talonflame and pressures Fairies. Kingambit Sucker Punch picks Dragapult, Shuca survives Garchomp EQ. Sinistcha Rage Powder + Strength Sap redirects and cripples Garchomp/Annihilape to protect Gengar. Dragonite and Staraptor provide dual Tailwind, Intimidate and Multiscale to control speed and blunt physical offense, with Ice Punch and Brave Bird for Garchomp/Altaria/Meganium.

Mega Floette's Fairy Aura Light of Ruin is the primary nuke, OHKOing Dragonite (after Multiscale break) and threatening most neutral targets. Dragapult outspeeds everything including Mega Gengar and pressures it with Life Orb Shadow Ball. Annihilape's Defiant punishes Staraptor's Intimidate while Close Combat guarantees the OHKO on Kingambit. Talonflame provides priority Tailwind to flip speed tiers for Floette and Garchomp. Rotom-Wash is the bulky pivot spreading burns and checking Camerupt. Garchomp pressures with spread Earthquake and Rock Slide flinches.

Lead with Mega Charizard Y to set sun and cancel opponent's rain, neutering Mega Swampert's Swift Swim and boosting our Fire/Grass moves. Whimsicott provides Prankster Tailwind and Encore to control speed and lock opponents into setup. Archaludon and Galarian Stunfisk handle Water and Electric threats with Thunderbolt and Earthquake, while Grimmsnarl sets dual screens with Prankster to protect the team. Quaquaval cleans up with Aqua Step and Close Combat, benefiting from speed boosts and hitting Dark/Fire types hard.

Rain core of Pelipper + Mega Swampert counters Mega Charizard Y by resetting weather with Rain Dance after Drought activates and OHKOing with Swift Swim Waterfall (88-262%). Incineroar's Intimidate + Fake Out provides universal support and is immune to Meta's Psychic STAB. Gholdengo's Steel/Ghost typing makes it immune to Quaquaval's Close Combat and Shadow Ball hits Mega Metagross for SE (42-113%). Farigiraf's Armor Tail shuts down all opposing priority including Prankster from Whimsicott/Grimmsnarl, while Trick Room offers alternative speed control. Klefki provides dual screens to keep the team alive against Meta's physical onslaught and Thunder Wave for speed disruption.

Altaria's Cloud Nine shuts down Pelipper's Drizzle, neutralising Mega Swampert's Swift Swim and letting the rest of the team outrun it. Mega Floette and Rotom-Wash pressure the rain core — Floette OHKOs Swampert with Energy Ball while Rotom deletes Pelipper with Thunderbolt. Annihilape punishes Incineroar's Intimidate with Defiant and Taunt stops Trick Room or screens. Garchomp cleans up Gholdengo and Incineroar with Life Orb Earthquake, and Dragapult offers unmatched speed, burns, and a pivot.

Rain core: Pelipper sets Drizzle (extended by Damp Rock) and Tailwind, enabling Swampert-Mega's Swift Swim to outspeed the entire meta including Dragapult. Gholdengo is the primary Mega Floette answer—Steel typing resists Fairy and Make It Rain hits SE. Incineroar's Fake Out chips Talonflame below full HP to disable Gale Wings while Intimidate softens physical attackers like Garchomp and Annihilape. Houndoom with Focus Sash provides a secondary Floette answer via Sludge Bomb and Dark STAB for Ghost-types. Farigiraf's Armor Tail passively blocks all opponent priority (insurance vs Gale Wings Brave Bird) and offers Helping Hand/Ally Switch support.
